facts.statement: Iberosuchus, meaning "Iberian crocodile," is an extinct genus of sebecosuchian mesoeucrocodylian found in Western Europe during the Eocene.
facts.quote: Iberosuchus (meaning "Iberian crocodile") is a genus of extinct sebecosuchian mesoeucrocodylian found in Western Europe from the Eocene.

facts.statement: Remains of Iberosuchus from Portugal were described in 1975 by Antunes as a sebecosuchian crocodilian.
facts.quote: Remains from Portugal was described in 1975 by Antunes as a sebecosuchian crocodilian.

facts.statement: The genus Iberosuchus contains only one species, I. macrodon, which means "large-toothed."
facts.quote: This genus has one species: I. macrodon (meaning "large toothed).

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodilians, Iberosuchus was a terrestrial animal rather than an aquatic one.
facts.quote: Unlike the crocodilians today, they were not aquatic but were instead terrestrial.

facts.statement: Iberosuchus was a carnivore.
facts.quote: Iberosuchus was a carnivore.

facts.statement: Robert Carroll reclassified Iberosuchus as a baurusuchid in 1988.
facts.quote: It was reclassified as a baurusuchid by Robert Carroll in 1988.

facts.statement: Iberosuchus possessed ziphodont teeth with laterally compressed crowns and distally curved apices.
facts.quote: Iberosuchus has ziphodont teeth that have a laterally compressed tooth crown that had a distally curved apex

facts.statement: The dorsal osteoderms of Iberosuchus were anterior-posteriorly elongated with a keel running through the central median.
facts.quote: anterior-posteriorly elongated dorsal osteoderms that have a keel running through the central median

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Iberosuchus featured rugose ornamentations without pits or cupules.
facts.quote: rugose ornamentations with no pits and cupules

facts.statement: The skull of Iberosuchus had a vermiculated texture.
facts.quote: the skull is vermiculated

facts.statement: Iberosuchus had a spoon-like premaxilla palatal shelf or mandibular symphysis.
facts.quote: spoon-like premaxilla palatal shelf or mandibular symphysis

facts.statement: Iberosuchus possessed a deep rostrum or mandible.
facts.quote: deep rostrum or mandible

facts.statement: Recovered teeth of Iberosuchus were labiolingually compressed with denticles along the edges, classifying them as ziphodont, and their crowns curved distally.
facts.quote: The teeth that are recovered are all labiolingually compressed with denticles along the edges, hence they are ziphodont, and the crown curves distally.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Iberosuchus featured a tall ridge surrounded by smaller ridges.
facts.quote: They have a tall ridge surrounded by smaller ridges.

facts.statement: In some smaller osteoderms, a central ridge joined with two accessory processes to form a cross shape in dorsal view.
facts.quote: In some smaller osteoderms, a ridge runs along the length of the osteoderm, joining with two smaller accessory processes and form a cross shape in the dorsal view

facts.statement: The first cranial remains of Iberosuchus were excavated from the Feligueira Grande Formation in the Leiria District of Portugal.
facts.quote: The first fossil of Ibersosuchus consisting of cranial remains was excavated in the Feligueira Grande Formation located in Praia de Vale Furado in the Leiria District of Portugal.

facts.statement: A mandibular element of Iberosuchus was found in Caenes, Spain, dating to the Bartonian age (roughly 44 to 39 million years ago).
facts.quote: The mandibular element was found in Caenes, Salamanca Province in Spain; it from the Bartonian age in MP 16 (mammal Paleogene zone), which is roughly 44 to 39 million years ago.

facts.statement: A snout fragment of Iberosuchus was found in the Tosalet del Morral of Lerida province, Spain, dating to the Lutetian age.
facts.quote: The other is snout fragment Tosalet del Morral of Lerida province in Spain, from the Lutetian age.

facts.statement: The oldest fossils of Iberosuchus found at the Aumelas site in France date back to the mid-Lutetian age (MP 13).
facts.quote: Aumelas site has the oldest fossils found at the site were dated back to mid Lutetian age, MP 13

facts.statement: Fossils of Iberosuchus from the Robiac site in France date to the Bartonian age (MP 16).
facts.quote: Robiac site was dated to be in the Bartonian age, MP 16.

facts.statement: Iberosuchus has synonyms including Atacisaurus (Astre, 1931) and Isselosaurus (Filhol, 1888).
facts.quote: synonyms: Atacisaurus Astre, 1931 Isselosaurus Filhol, 1888

facts.statement: Iberosuchus is an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylian sebecosuchian from Western Europe of the Eocene.
facts.quote: Iberosuchus (nombre que significa "cocodrilo de Iberia") es un género extinto de mesoeucrocodiliano sebecosuquio procedente del Eoceno de Europa Occidental.

facts.statement: Iberosuchus was described in 1975 by Antunes based on remains from Portugal as a sebecosuchian crocodile.
facts.quote: Fue descrito en 1975 por Antunes a partir de restos de Portugal como un cocodrilo sebecosuquio.

facts.statement: Iberosuchus lived between 56 and 33.9 million years ago during the Ypresian to Priabonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Priabonian (56 to 33.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Iberosuchus was a predator that lived on land rather than in water, unlike modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Iberosuchus era un depredador, pero a diferencia de los crocodilianos modernos, se considera que los sebecosuquios era animales terrestres, no acuáticos.

facts.statement: In 1996, Ortega and colleagues extended the range of Iberosuchus to France by reassigning the fragmentary species Atacisaurus crassiproratus to it.
facts.quote: su rango fue extendido a Francia en 1996 por Ortega y colaboradores, quienes reasignaron a la especie fragmentaria Atacisaurus crassiproratus como un ejemplar de Iberosuchus
